children: will be announcing earnings results this Monday before market hours. Here’s what to look for.
Marriott missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $7.07 billion, up 4.8% year on year. It was a mixed quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Marriott a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Marriott’s revenue to grow 6.9% year on year, improving from the 3.7% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Marriott has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Marriott’s peers in the consumer discretionary - travel and vacation providers segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Hilton Grand Vacations delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 50.8%, beating analysts’ expectations by 39.5%, and Frontier reported revenues up 52.9%, topping estimates by 4.9%. Hilton Grand Vacations traded up 8.2% following the results while Frontier was also up 17.2%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the consumer discretionary - travel and vacation providers segment, with share prices up 3.2% on average over the last month. Marriott is up 8.8% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $387.77 (compared to the current share price of $390.50).
